key_insight: Compute a geometry-aware reward in 4D latent space (space + time) to align pretrained video diffusion models to world-consistent generation, avoiding architectural changes and costly RGB reconstructions.
problem_solved: Video diffusion models produce high-quality frames but often violate geometric/temporal consistency; prior fixes either alter model architectures (hurting generalization) or use RGB-space alignment that is slow and limited to static scenes.
method: Design a 4D (3D space + time) latent reward that measures world-consistency across frames inside the model's latent space rather than in decoded RGB.
Use the latent reward to guide optimization/alignment of pretrained video diffusion models (reward-based policy/optimization) without adding new generation modules.
Operate entirely in latent space to support dynamic scenes and avoid repeated VAE decoding, reducing compute and preserving internet-scale pretraining generalization.
impact: Enables efficient, architecture-preserving refinement of pretrained video diffusion models for better geometric and temporal consistency, making high-quality, world-consistent video generation practical for researchers and production systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained video diffusion model -> 4D latent extractor -> latent reward computation -> reward-guided optimization (no new modules).
Before/after frame sequence illustrating improved geometric consistency across frames (e.g., stable camera/object geometry).
Bar/line chart comparing consistency metrics and compute cost: RGB-space alignment vs 4D latent reward (show lower cost and higher consistency).
Conceptual 4D visualization (space-time cube) showing how rewards link spatial geometry across time rather than per-frame RGB errors.
paper_title: VGGRPO: Towards World-Consistent Video Generation with 4D Latent Reward
paper_authors: Zhaochong An, Orest Kupyn, Théo Uscidda, Andrea Colaco, Karan Ahuja
